in_text_mentions: Sonographic examination demonstrated hepatomegaly, measuring upto 12 cm. Antero-inferior beaking of second, third, and fourth lumbar vertebrae was noted on skeletal survey (Figure 2). Bilateral thalami were hyperdense on CT (Figure 3) and showed T1 hyperintensity and T2 hypointensity (Figure 4A and B). The anterior limb of the internal capsule, bilateral lobar and periventricular white matter, and subcortical U fibres in the frontal lobes show T2 hyperintensity on MRI; the T1 signal alterations were isointense, which suggested hypomyelination (Figure 5). panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Clinical photograph of the face in a 12-month-old infant with infantile GM1 gangliosidosis. The caption explicitly describes coarse facial features, a recognized GM1 manifestation. Redaction bar over eyes and panel label are present. [raw subtype: infantile] B: Clinical photograph of the back showing extensive dermal melanocytosis in an infant with infantile GM1 gangliosidosis. The finding is not in the supplied vocabulary, so it is listed as a proposed finding. [raw subtype: infantile] C: Clinical photograph of the gluteal region showing extensive dermal melanocytosis in an infant with infantile GM1 gangliosidosis. The finding is not in the supplied vocabulary, so it is listed as a proposed finding. [raw subtype: infantile]

panels.figure_caption: (A) Coarse facial features in a 12-month-old infant. (B and C) Extensive dermal melanocytosis of back and gluteal region.
in_text_mentions: Upon physical examination, the back and gluteal region showed variable sized bluish pigmentation which suggested significant cutaneous melanocytosis (Figure 1B and C), lowset ears, coarse facial features, a depressed nasal bridge, and an increased intercanthal distance (Figure 1A). Head appeared enlarged as per age. Head circumference was 51.5 cm (>97 percentile). It was discovered that the remaining anthropometric measurements fell within normal bounds.
